title: Evaluation-compatible external duality respects a structural comparison
statement:
Use finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, correspondences $c:C\to X\times_kX$ and $\bar c:\bar C\to\bar X\times_k\bar X$ of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and a cohomological pre-comparison $(f_Z,t_Z,\alpha_g,\beta_g,\iota)$ with notation $r_Z,d_Z,\delta_Z,j_Z,\Pi$ as in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. Assume axioms (I)--(V) of that definition, the exceptional tensor identity (a), tensor-unit identity (c), and dualizing projection identity (d) displayed in [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus]; the latter identities are hypotheses here, without requiring compactifiability. All exceptional operations and complexes used are in the admissible finite-Tor constructible domains of [def-trf-admissibility]. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ put $K'=f_XK$ and
$$P=K\boxtimes D_XK,\quad Q=f_XK\boxtimes f_XD_XK,\quad\bar P=K'\boxtimes D_{\bar X}K',\quad J=1\boxtimes d_X:Q\to\bar P,$$
$$V=R\mathcal Hom(p_2^*K,p_1^!K),\quad\bar V=R\mathcal Hom(\bar p_2^*K',\bar p_1^!K'),\quad\theta=R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_{p_2},\beta_{p_1})\circ r_{X\times X}:f_{X\times X}V\to\bar V.$$
Here $D_X$ is Verdier duality [def-trf-dualizing-complex], the $p_i$ and $\bar p_i$ are the two product projections, and $\kappa:P\to V$, $\bar\kappa:\bar P\to\bar V$ are exactly the evaluation-defined maps of [def-sf-kv-maps](iv). Then
$$\theta\circ f_{X\times X}(\kappa)\circ\Pi_{K,D_XK}=\bar\kappa\circ J:Q\longrightarrow\bar V.$$
This identity holds whether or not $\Pi_{K,D_XK}$ is invertible; it compares the maps before cancellation and has no trace-class conclusion.

source.place: §4.4.3, left square of (4.12) and diagrams (4.14)--(4.15), with the two legs interchanged

proof.text:
Put $F=f_{X\times X}$, $f=f_X$, and write $\bar p_i$ for the projections on $\bar X\times\bar X$. Tensor--Hom uncurrying tests the desired equality after tensoring $Q$ with $\bar p_2^*K'$. With the signed symmetry, use the common source
$$S=\bar p_2^*fD_XK\otimes\bar p_2^*fK\otimes\bar p_1^*fK$$
and target $\bar p_1^!fK$. The uncurrying of $\theta F(\kappa)\Pi$ first applies the three ordinary comparisons, combines them by $t_{X\times X}$, applies $F$ to second-factor evaluation followed by $\alpha_{\operatorname{id}_X,a_X}$, and finally applies $\beta_{p_1}(K)$. This follows by expanding $r_{X\times X}$ and $\Pi$ from [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], naturality of $t$, and associativity and signed commutativity (I). The uncurrying of $\bar\kappa J$ applies $\bar p_2^*d_X$ to the dual factor, evaluates that factor against $\bar p_2^*fK$, then applies the barred exceptional Künneth map with $\bar p_1^*fK$. These descriptions are exactly [def-sf-kv-maps](iii),(iv). They are diagram (4.14) with BOTH projection indices interchanged; in particular the exceptional target is indexed by $1$, not $2$.

source.place: §4.4.3, reduction of the left square of (4.12) to the uncurried maps and diagram (4.14)

proof.text:
Write $e:D_XK\otimes K\to\omega_X$ for evaluation. Apply axiom (IV) of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] to $g=p_2$ and $M=D_XK,N=K$. Its well-typed equation is
$$\alpha_{p_2}(M\otimes N)\circ\bar p_2^*t_X(M,N)
=t_{X\times X}(p_2^*M,p_2^*N)\circ(\alpha_{p_2}(M)\otimes\alpha_{p_2}(N)).$$
Naturality of $\alpha_{p_2}$ for $e$ identifies the first tensor/evaluation segment of the unbarred route with $\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)\circ\bar p_2^*(f(e)\circ t_X)$. Tensor with the remaining factor $\bar p_1^*fK$; associativity of $t$ in (I) makes this the left square of the factor-swapped (4.14). Thus it remains to compare the exceptional segments on
$$B=\bar p_2^*f\omega_X\otimes\bar p_1^*fK.$$
No exceptional-tensor theorem is used in this step.

source.place: §4.4.3, left inner square of (4.14), with both projection indices interchanged

proof.text:
Let $T=T_{p_1}$ and $\chi:p_2^*\omega_X\to p_1^!A_X$. By [lem-trf-projection-kunneth-tensor], the unbarred exceptional Künneth map, after the signed swap, is $T\circ(\chi\otimes1)$; the barred map has the identical description. The unbarred exceptional segment on $B$ is therefore
$$L=\beta_{p_1}(K)\circ F(T)\circ t_{X\times X}\circ(F(\chi)\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)\otimes\alpha_{p_1}(K)).$$
Naturality of $t$ and identity (a) of [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus], used as an ASSUMED identity at $g=p_1,M=A_X,N=K$, give
$$L=\bar p_1^!(t_X)\circ T_{\bar p_1}\circ(\beta_{p_1}(A_X)F(\chi)\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)\otimes1).$$
Substitute the assumed identity (d), then use naturality of $T_{\bar p_1}$ in its first argument, to obtain
$$L=\bar p_1^!\bigl(t_X\circ(j_X\otimes1)\bigr)\circ T_{\bar p_1}\circ(\bar\chi\,\bar p_2^*\delta_X\otimes1)
=T_{\bar p_1}\circ(\bar\chi\,\bar p_2^*\delta_X\otimes1).$$
The last equality is the assumed tensor-unit identity (c); its left-unit version follows from signed commutativity (I). All displayed equalities include the canonical unit and signed symmetry identifications. This proves the exceptional square of the factor-swapped (4.15). Finally the definition of $d_X$ as $r_X$ followed by $\delta_X$ gives, by its evaluation transpose,
$$\delta_X\circ f(e)\circ t_X(D_XK,K)=\operatorname{ev}_{fK}\circ(d_X\otimes1).$$
Combining this with Step 2 identifies the full unbarred route with the uncurrying of $\bar\kappa J$. Compactifiability is not invoked: only the identities (a),(c),(d) explicitly assumed in the item are used.

source.place: §4.4.3, diagrams (4.14)--(4.15), with both projection indices interchanged; Lemma 4.2.4(b),(f), Lemma 4.2.2(a), and (0.4)

proof.text: The two uncurried composites are equal by Steps 2 and 3. The tensor–Hom uncurrying map is injective, so the original morphisms $\theta\,f_{X\times X}(\kappa)\,\Pi_{K,D_XK}$ and $\bar\kappa\,J$ are equal. The argument compares the maps before any cancellation and therefore remains valid when $\Pi_{K,D_XK}$ is not an isomorphism; no trace-class assertion is used.
